CAN.note: World's #1 rapeseed/canola seed exporter. StatCan MY2024/25 production ~19.2 Mt; record domestic crush ~9.6-11.5 Mt; seed exports ~9.5 Mt with China #1 (~4.6 Mt MY24/25; ~5.9 Mt calendar 2024), Japan ~1.7 Mt, EU ~1.1 Mt, Mexico ~0.8 Mt, UAE ~0.57 Mt (StatCan/Canola Council 2024).

AUS.note: World's #2 canola/rapeseed seed exporter; non-GM premium crop. ABARES 2024 crop ~6.45 Mt; exports ~6.13 Mt (yr to Sep 2024) led by Japan ~1.33 Mt, then EU (Germany, Belgium, France) and Pakistan. Not selling to China since 2020 (blackleg dispute) (ABARES/Grain Central 2024).

UKR.note: Major rapeseed exporter and large sunflower-seed grower (seed mostly crushed domestically). USDA MY2024/25 rapeseed exports ~2.6-3.6 Mt, ~80%+ to the EU (Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, France); sunflower-seed exports only ~0.3 Mt as Ukraine crushes its own (USDA FAS Kyiv 2024).

RUS.note: World's largest sunflower-seed producer and a major rapeseed grower, but a partial seed export ban (rapeseed exempt only for the China-bordering Far East; sunflower seed effectively blocked) keeps most seed in domestic crush. Seed exports modest; rapeseed to China and Kazakhstan (USDA FAS / APK-Inform 2024).

FRA.note: EU's largest rapeseed grower and a major crusher; both exports intra-EU seed (to Germany, Belgium, Spain) and imports for its crush. 2024 rapeseed crop reduced by wet weather (FAOSTAT 2024; USDA/EU Commission 2024).

DEU.note: Europe's biggest rapeseed crusher and the largest single seed importer. 2024 imports ~6-7 Mt rapeseed/canola from Ukraine, Australia, Canada, France, plus intra-EU; feeds biodiesel and food-oil crush (FAOSTAT 2024; EU Commission oilseeds 2024).

CHN.note: World's largest rapeseed importer for crush. USDA: rapeseed-seed imports ~3.7 Mt (2024) plus large canola flows from Canada; calendar-2024 Canadian canola seed alone ~5.9 Mt. Domestic rapeseed output ~15 Mt is the world's largest but far short of consumption ~18.5 Mt (USDA FAS 2024).

IND.note: World's #3 rapeseed (mustard) producer ~11-12 Mt, near self-sufficient in the seed, but the largest sunflower-SEED importer (~26% of world sunflower-seed imports 2024). Imports planting/crush sunflower seed; exports rapeseed meal (USDA FAS / ITC 2024).

BEL.note: Antwerp/Ghent crush-and-transit hub. Imports rapeseed/canola from Ukraine, Australia, Canada and France, crushes and re-exports seed onward to Germany and the Netherlands (FAOSTAT 2024).

NLD.note: Rotterdam entrepot: imports rapeseed (Ukraine, Australia, France, Romania) and re-exports ~1 Mt onward, chiefly to Germany. Negligible own production; pure trade/crush node (FAOSTAT 2024).

ROU.note: Largest Black-Sea EU rapeseed and sunflower-seed exporter. 2024 seed shipped to Bulgaria, Netherlands, France, Germany, Hungary, Portugal and Pakistan; also a sunflower-seed exporter via Constanta (FAOSTAT 2024).

HUN.note: Central-European rapeseed and sunflower-seed exporter; ships seed to Austria, Germany, Italy and neighbours, while importing some from Romania/Croatia (FAOSTAT 2024).

POL.note: Large EU rapeseed grower and crusher; exports surplus seed to Germany and the Czech Republic and imports from Czechia/Slovakia/Lithuania for its crush plants (FAOSTAT 2024).

BGR.note: Black-Sea rapeseed and sunflower-seed grower and re-exporter. 2024 imports from Romania and Moldova, exports to Netherlands, Germany, China and the UK; mixed rapeseed/sunflower seed (FAOSTAT 2024).

MDA.note: Outsized rapeseed and sunflower-seed exporter for its size; 2024 seed shipped to Romania, Bulgaria, Turkey and Greece (FAOSTAT 2024).

JPN.note: Pure net importer; no domestic rapeseed/canola. 2024 imports ~2.3-2.4 Mt canola/rapeseed seed for crush, split mainly between Australia (~1.14 Mt) and Canada (~0.96 Mt) (FAOSTAT 2024; Comtrade 2024).

PAK.note: Growing net importer of canola/rapeseed seed for its crush; 2024 imports ~0.7-0.8 Mt led by Australia (~0.65 Mt) and Romania (FAOSTAT 2024).

rankings.note: Rapeseed/canola seed (HS1205) + sunflower seed (HS1206) basket, kt, 2024, blending USDA FAS Oilseeds PSD, StatCan/ABARES national data and FAOSTAT 2024 importer-reports. Canada and Australia dominate seed exports; Germany, China, Japan, Belgium and the Netherlands lead seed imports (China the largest rapeseed importer; the EU the largest crush bloc). NOTE 2024: this is the SEED basket - distinct from soybeans and from vegetable oils/meals; rapeseed dominates the traded seed, sunflower seed is mostly crushed at origin (Ukraine, Russia, Argentina) so its traded volumes are smaller.

companies.name: Cargill
companies.note: Among the world's largest oilseed crushers and traders; operates major canola crush plants in Canada (incl. Camrose, Clavet) and rapeseed crush in the EU. Originates Canadian/Australian/Black-Sea seed for crush into oil and meal (Cargill 2024).
companies.improve: Should publish plant-level canola/rapeseed origination by province/region and deforestation- and labour-risk screening for its Black-Sea and Australian seed supply (2024).

companies.name: Bunge Global
companies.note: Global oilseed processor; large EU and Canadian rapeseed/canola crush footprint, expanded via the 2024-25 Viterra combination which deepened its Canadian canola origination (Bunge 2024).
companies.improve: Should disclose merged Bunge-Viterra canola origination concentration in Western Canada and sustainability sourcing standards for EU rapeseed crush (2024).

companies.name: Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM)
companies.note: Major oilseed crusher with canola plants in Canada (Lloydminster, Windsor) and rapeseed crush across the EU; trades and processes Black-Sea and North American seed (ADM 2024).
companies.improve: Should report canola/rapeseed crush capacity utilisation and traceability for Ukrainian/Black-Sea seed origination amid wartime supply risk (2024).

companies.name: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC)
companies.note: Top-tier oilseed merchant; trades Canadian canola, Australian non-GM canola and Black-Sea rapeseed/sunflower seed, with crush assets in the EU and Canada (LDC 2024).
companies.improve: Should disclose origin-level volumes and ESG screening for its Australian and Black-Sea seed flows, and water/energy intensity of EU crush (2024).

companies.name: Viterra
companies.note: Canada's leading grain/canola handler and a major canola crusher (Ste. Agathe, expanding Regina plant); a dominant node in Western-Canadian canola origination and export, now combining with Bunge (Viterra 2024).
companies.improve: Should publish farm-gate canola origination concentration in Saskatchewan/Alberta and the competitive effects of the Bunge merger on grower pricing (2024).

companies.name: Richardson International
companies.note: Canada's largest agribusiness fully owned domestically; a leading canola handler and crusher (Yorkton, Lethbridge) feeding both export seed and canola-oil processing (Richardson 2024). Flagged modeled: no FoodShield company source file yet.
companies.improve: Should disclose canola crush capacity and origination footprint by province and its share of Western-Canadian farmer deliveries (2024).

global.note: World rapeseed/canola + sunflower SEED totals, kt, USDA FAS Oilseeds PSD (rapeseed ~88 Mt + sunflower seed ~55 Mt = ~143 Mt output 2024/25). Trade is dominated by rapeseed/canola SEED (~18-20 Mt) plus smaller sunflower-seed flows; most sunflower seed is crushed at origin so global seed trade is modest relative to output. EU is the largest crush bloc; China the largest rapeseed-seed importer (USDA / EU Commission 2024).

forecast.method: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook envelope; 2030=2024x(1+rate)^6. Rapeseed/canola seed output and trade grow modestly on EU/Canada/India crush demand, tempered by EU biofuel-policy softening and China-Canada canola trade frictions; sunflower seed stays origin-crushed.
